title: OpenPiton (PrincetonUniversity/openpiton)
_note: Princeton's OpenPiton manycore: the tile (its OpenSPARC T1-derived core,
the L1.5 and L2 caches and the dynamic-node NoC routers), the chip bridge,
the JTAG block, the chipset (memory and I/O controllers, the crossbars) and
the common cells.
Why it needs a generation step at all -- this is what 'the config closure is
the work' on docs/todo.md meant.  91 files under piton/design are PyHP
TEMPLATES (`*.pyv`) that OpenPiton's build preprocesses into `*.tmp.h` /
`*.tmp.v`, and the design `include`s the generated headers by bare name
(define.tmp.h, ifu.tmp.h, l15.tmp.h, l2.tmp.h, lsu.tmp.h), so without the
step every file that includes one is unreadable.
The generation turns out to need NO configuration: pyhp.py takes its
defaults from piton/tools/bin/pyhplib.py, so `pyhp.py <in>.pyv >
<out>.tmp.<ext>` per file is the whole flow -- the same command OpenPiton's
own FuseSoC preprocessor runs, with the output names following the
`process_me` pairs in its .core files (strip `.pyv`, then `.h`/`.v` becomes
`.tmp.h`/`.tmp.v`).
piton/design/fpga_tests is skipped by the generator: its
mem_test_par_driver.v.pyv still contains a PYTHON 2 `print` statement, so
pyhp.py raises a SyntaxError on it.  OpenPiton's own design flow never
processes that tree (an FPGA memory-test harness, not design RTL) and the
family does not sweep it.
The generated headers are always_srcs AND the family reads --single-unit,
for the same reason OpenC910 does: OpenPiton's build compiles the headers
ahead of the design, and plenty of files USE their macros without
`include`ing them -- sparc_exu_alu.v includes nothing at all and reads
`L1D_ADDRESS_HI` from lsu.tmp.h, so Surelog reports
`[ERR:PA0203] Unknown macro` and the row cannot elaborate; read_slang loses
the same macros across compilation units without --single-unit.
First local sweep 2026-10-27 (852 rows, MEM_LIMIT_KB=7000000 as the nightly
uses): 646 / 838 comparable proven, 670 / 838 elaborate, 576 co-sim PASS,
688 rows with 0 undriven, 3.3 h of row time.
Two leads, both worth working from the nightly:
* 61 rows read-FAIL with
`ERROR: Multiple edge sensitive events found for this signal!`, and this is
NOT a reader defect -- it was first recorded here as one, wrongly.  yosys
cannot infer an asynchronous reset from a TERNARY at all: OpenPiton's flop
library writes
always @ (posedge clk or posedge rst)
q <= rst ? {SIZE{1'b0}} : din;
and proc_dff emits that exact message for read_verilog TOO, while
read_slang refuses the shape outright ('simple if-else pattern expected in
modeling an asynchronous load on a flip-flop').  Rewritten to
`if (rst) ... else ...` all three accept it and read_uhdm emits a clean
$adff.  Seven cells in chip/tile/common/rtl/swrvr_clib.v use the idiom
(dffr_async, dffr_async_ns, dffr_async_ns_r1, dffr_async_ns_cl_r1,
dffrl_async, dffrl_async_ns, dffsl_async_ns) plus chipset net_int_sync,
and every module instantiating one inherits the failure -- lsu, sparc_ifu,
sparc_exu_ecl, fpu_mul, jtag and most of the core.
A generation-time source rewrite was written and ABANDONED: the bodies sit
behind `ifndef YOSYS directives that a line-oriented rewriter folds into
the `if`, and the active-low cells condition on (!rst_l), whose negation a
naive rewrite DROPS -- inverting the reset and making the sweep measure
fabricated RTL.  Doing it safely needs a Verilog-aware transform, so these
rows are left failing and honestly accounted for rather than measured
against rewritten source.
* 78 rows cannot elaborate, and the whole-system ones (chip, chipset,
chipset_impl, l2, l2_mshr_decoder) all fail the same way: Surelog reports
`[ERR:PP0115] Recursive macro definition for "XY_WIDTH"` on
include/network_define.v, where that macro is defined EXACTLY ONCE as a
literal (`define XY_WIDTH 8`), and every macro defined after the
diagnostic is then reported unknown (L2_MSHR_SRC_FBITS_LO and friends),
which is what the syntax errors downstream are.  A plain duplicate
`define` does NOT reproduce it, so the trigger is the double-include
path (define.tmp.h includes network_define.v, and the design includes
both) rather than redefinition as such: a Surelog preprocessor lead.
MEASURED both ways -- these rows fail identically with and without the
generated headers in always_srcs, so always_srcs is not the cause; it is
kept because it is strictly better (sparc_exu_alu is proven with it and
cannot elaborate without it, and nothing else changes).
The rest: 11 `differs` rows of which 8 also diverge in co-simulation, 13
SAT-budget rows (8 timeout, 5 over the memory cap), and 15 rows with no
read_slang reference.
